sections.text: This shalt thou learn by prostrating thyself at the Masters feet, by questioning Him and by serving Him. The wise who have realised the Truth will teach thee wisdom.
Having known That, thou shalt never again be confounded; and, O Arjuna, by the power of that wisdom, thou shalt see all these people as if they were thine own Self, and therefore as Me.
Be thou the greatest of sinners, yet thou shalt cross over all sin by the ferryboat of wisdom.

What is my purpose and destiny? We have been discussing chapter four, Gnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga Yoga of renouncing action in knowledge. So we have seen in the beginning of chapter three, Bhagavan had said that there are two paths always available for a seeker to seek the ultimate knowledge. The Gnana Yogi in a Sankhyana Karma Yoga yogina. For the yogis, the Karma Yoga and for the Gnani, the Gnana Yoga. So chapter three we discussed Karma Yoga.
This is where one needs to start. Bhagavan Saha that if you are engaged in this world of activities, in this rajasic world of activities, then it will start with Karma Yoga. And Karma Yoga simply says act with the balanced mind without expecting any particular fruits of your action and act efficiently. Thats basically Karma Yoga. Remain balanced in any situation. Do not react overly in any situation.
Bhagawan said, you start with that. Purpose of that is to purify your mind and intellectual so that you can function very efficiently in this world. But what type of action I should be performing in that manner was described in chapter four. In the beginning, Bhagawan said, you should know what is karma and what is akarma. You should know what is vikarma, what is akarma. So you should have some basic gauge to decide actions are appropriate or not appropriate there.
Bhagavan said that when you reach a point where action seems inaction and inaction seems action, you now come to understand what action is all about. And how do I get to that point? Bhagavan said, Yajnaar Thaat Karmano Anyatra Lokwayam Karma Bandana. You get bondage from your action in this world because you are acting in this world as an individual trying to compete with the rest of the world. Its creating sorrows and unhappiness and fears and greed and jealousy. Thats because this concept of duality that I am an island by myself, the world is out there to get me.
Bhagwan said that you overcome by performing your Actions in the field of Yajna. Yajna is something youre not doing for yourself. Youre sacrificing something for greater good. So if you go to Hindu temple and Panditji is doing Havana, every mantra start with Idhamna Mama, this is not mine. Up till now I thought this is mine. But right now Im offering it for the greater good in the holy fire.
Something I always thought is mine -- I offer it as no longer belonging to me. That is what we call charity. The money which I thought is mine, I write a check and send it to a non-profit organization. I say, Now it is not mine, it is yours. You do whatever you need to do. So thats the act of Yajna.
Yajna is to sacrifice something which you thought is yours. But you came to the conclusion that really does not belong to me. I heard one of the CNN executive retiring and he said learn, earn and then return. Learn the knowledge, how the business works. Then earn, make money and then return. Return back to the community.
And thats what most of us one way or other do. Because we have seen that when a person dies, he cannot take anything with him. He acquires things, thinks they are his own, and then eventually gives up, leaves everything here and goes away. So Bhagavan said that you have to understand this concept even while acting in this world. Therefore you have to act in the spirit of Yajna so that you come to realize the oneness. Once you perform this, you will get the Brahmajnana. I have this translation of Gnaneshwar Maharajs Gnaneshwari.
This chapter is actually titled in Gnaneshwari as Brahma Yajna Prasantsa Brahmajna Prasansa Nama Chaturtha Dhyayah. So here we say Gnana Karma Sanyasi Yogana. There are books I have seen which simply says Gnani Yoga. So chapter four is about knowledge. Knowledge about your own self and how to get it. So the two paths which Bhagavan had initially described that is always available right from the beginning of this universe for a seeker to realize the truth is Karma Yoga.
And then Gnana Yoga, Karma Yoga. When you are not ready yet, very Rajasic, perform Karma Yoga. But then ultimately you have to have Gnana. The knowledge, what it is all about, why my actions are not my actions. And when I come to realize, it becomes inaction. Its no longer any action which is belonging to me.
So in verse 33 we say, Sarvam karma akhilam Partha gnane parisamapyate. Bhagavan came to that final statement saying, O Partha. All the actions, good, bad and ugly that you had been performing or you think you had been performing once you know the knowledge, they get all dissolved once you achieve their knowledge. What is their knowledge? He said we would learn that. Brahma arpanam Brahmahavihi Brahma agno Brahmahutam.
Everything that I perceive in this world that I consider to be something other than me is also not different than me. The same entity which makes me who I am, the very same entity makes the world of plurality what it is. Once I come to that conclusion, Bhagavan said, Sarvam karma akhilam grana parishama pyyade. All actions which I am either very proud of or very afraid of that I may have to pay for them. Those actions all will get resolved. So in last verse 34, Bhagavan said, the only way to get it is to someone who has realized this knowledge.
I can only learn something from someone who has experienced it. If I am dreaming and suffering in my dream, only other waker can see that I may be going through a nightmare and awake me. Are you having a nightmare? Another dreamer cannot do that. Another dreamer who is also dreaming his own dream. He cannot wake me up from my dream.
Only a waker who is not dreaming can see that I am having a nightmare and can wake me up. So Bhagavan said, go to a guru. You may not call them a guru -- you may give them another title. But go to someone who has experienced this knowledge, someone who has experienced this truth that there is no duality in this world. The world is the manifestation of the same reality.
That duality is created out of my own ignorance about the nature of this universe. In Prakriti there is multiplicity. Prakriti itself is one entity. But in that there is multiplicity. Just as I as one person. But I have multiple limbs which has different parts and different functions.
But I know that all these limbs are nothing but me. And therefore there is no conflict ever. My right hand is not fighting with left hand and left hand is not fighting with my right hand. Because there is a unity of thinking. And that knowledge, you can only get it from a great person who has realized this Tadviddhi Prani pati ne pari prasnayana sevaya. You have to put your own efforts.
You cant really get it just by thinking about it. You have to put your own efforts with that humility that you do not know. Right now, what I know is creating more conflict for me, creating sorrows, unhappiness, fears, jealousy, greed -- all of that. Because I think the world is out there to get me and I need to take care of myself. So once you know -- Tadviddhi Prani Patena Pari Prashnena -- by inquiring what is real and what is unreal, what is my true self and what is not my true self.
Sevayah -- by serving the teacher. Upadekshyanti Tegnanam Gnaninah Tattvadarsinah. And if you find that person -- if you are sincere, you will find such a person -- that teacher will point you in the right direction, will give you the direction on how to find your own self. You have to find yourself, but you will find a guide to get to your destination. Now, is this something Ill know one time and then forget?
There are a lot of things I have learnt before but have now forgotten -- that is of no great value. Rajan, do you know calculus? I learned it in my college days but I know nothing about it anymore. Bhagawan said no, this knowledge is different. Once you know it, you will never get confused like this again. You are right now confused about whether to fight or not to fight this battle.
Knowing that knowledge, you will never get confused again. Bhutani Ashena Drashasi Atmani Athomai. That is because right now my problem is that I see that world is competing with me and therefore Im getting confused about how to protect myself. And thats what is creating confusion. In Arjunas case, his own people are there and he has to kill them. He has no problem killing others, only his own people.
Hes worried about killing them. But once this sense of I and mine is dissolved, you will not have any problem. Two people facing each other in a dark alley are afraid of each other because one doesnt know who the other one is. So they hide from each other because they think the other person is out there to rob me. But once they realize that other person is my friend then all the fears are gone. So that identification is the unifying factor.
Bhagawan said, once that identification takes place -- Atmani Athomai -- you will see that all beings are in your own self. The self which I consider my own self is not limited to this body, mind and intellect. It is all-pervading and encompassing everything. That teacher will make you realize that your self is that supreme self where everything is contained. And you will see that in me -- me, Bhagavan said, meaning Krishna himself.
You will see in God all the beings. Thats nothing but your own self. When this takes place, all the fears will be dissolved, all the negative tendencies of your mind will dissolve, and you will be free from all the problems that belong to you.
So Bhagavan said Apiched -- now I come to the point of gauging my own capability. Am I capable of achieving this? And 99 times out of 100 we come to the conclusion: thats for the sannyasis, thats for somebody else, not for me.
It may be, but I dont know whether Im going to get it in this lifetime or not. Dont worry about the lifetime. Because you do not know what your lifetime is. This life is not the only existence you have. Bahuni, me, Vyatitani, Janmani, Tawachaljani. You and I have spent many, many lives before we never perished and we will be there forever.
So therefore time is not of any consequence here. Neither your own qualification. If you consider yourself the best among sinners -- even criminals have categories, the best and the worst, from a stupid criminal to the most intelligent criminal. All the jewel thief movies I used to love in my younger days.
Because jewel thief is not an ordinary person, he is so intelligent. If you consider that you are the worst of sinners, then also it does not exclude you. Because sin is nothing but the other aspect of karma. If it is utilized in a proper field, it becomes merit. If it is in a wrong field with a wrong attitude, it becomes sin. So all you are doing up till now is what you consider your sins is youre applying your ability to act with a wrong attitude.
Those attitudes and the consequent experiences are creating negative impressions on your mind. Therefore you consider yourself a sinner. But you cannot be a sinner, because you are part of that pristine reality.

Verse 34 prescribes the method for gaining knowledge: Tadviddhi pranipatena pariprashnena sevaya - learn it through prostration (humility), questioning, and service to those wise ones who have realized the truth (jnaninas tattva-darshinah). Verse 35 promises that having known this, you will never again fall into confusion, for you will see all beings in your own Self and in Me. The powerful verse 36 offers hope even to the greatest sinner: Api ched asi papebhyah sarvebhyah papa-krittamah - even if you are the worst of sinners, the boat of knowledge will carry you across all evil.
The teaching emphasizes that spiritual knowledge cannot be gained through intellect alone - it requires a relationship with a realized teacher and ones own sincere effort. Just as only a waking person can awaken someone from a nightmare (another dreamer cannot help), only one who has realized the truth can guide us out of our confusion. The three elements - prostration (humility), questioning (sincere inquiry), and service (devoted practice) - form the complete approach. Once this knowledge dawns, duality dissolves; you see all beings as your own Self because they truly are.
For todays practice, cultivate the three elements of learning. Practice humility by acknowledging what you do not know - your current knowledge is creating your confusion and suffering. Formulate genuine questions about what is real and unreal, what is your true Self and what is not. Serve the teaching through dedicated practice, not just intellectual study. Reflect on verse 35s promise: if you truly knew that all beings are in your Self and in God, how would you treat the people you encounter today? And take heart from verse 36 - whatever you consider your sins are merely actions performed with wrong attitudes. Your true Self, part of pristine reality, cannot be a sinner. The boat of knowledge can carry you across any ocean of past mistakes.
